8. Authentication: a concrete ambiguity in pooled mass analysis

I executed a separate observability calculation.

Consider P07 and P08:

Plain text
CAAAABBBBDAAAAABBBBB
CBBBBAAAADBBBBBAAAAA

Exchange their tails after residue nine:

Plain text
CAAAABBBBDBBBBBAAAAA
CBBBBAAAADAAAAABBBBB

The latter pair contains wrong-order products. Yet the two pairs have exactly the same pooled multiset of:

Parent compositions.
Every prefix-fragment composition.
Every suffix-fragment composition.

Replacing two equal-abundance members of the sixteen-product library would therefore create 12.5% wrong sequences while preserving that ideal aggregate mass-fragment readout.

This is not a claim that calibrated chromatography, ion mobility, actual fragment intensities or further fragmentation cannot distinguish the products. It establishes that pooled composition ladders alone do not authenticate sequence.

A real twenty-residue peptoid MS/MS decoding workflow exists, but its charge-enhancing architecture, multiple spectra and ambiguity handling do not automatically provide quantitative analysis of this dye-bearing, same-mass library. 
PMC

The necessary qualification method therefore includes:

Separate analysis of each cartridge’s released population.
A known-proportion pooled sample containing all sixteen products.
Independently prepared target, scrambled, deletion and wrong-linkage standards.
Calibrated recovery and response factors.
Minority spikes at relevant error levels.
Tests for coelution and ambiguous fragments.
Absolute molar recovery, not uncalibrated MS or fluorescence intensity.

The analytical method is an unresolved common requirement for both the proposed machine and its ordinary-synthesis comparator.
